approved_requirement: Maintainer requested a complete Rust rewrite plan on 2026-10-15: no backend Python; optional client-only Python permitted; native gateway and ssx included. This publication authorizes planning, not production deployment.
dependency_semantics: Every depends_on edge is a hard finish-to-start gate: predecessor implementation/decision/evidence must be accepted and merged before dependent implementation starts. Analysis may happen early but cannot claim readiness. Epic hierarchy is not a dependency.

items.title: Freeze parity inventory and the Python removal boundary
items.problem: The rewrite needs an executable definition of complete; source counts and old AGENTS descriptions are insufficient.
scope: Inventory every runtime entrypoint, adapter, route/format, MCP tool/resource/prompt, config default, state record, CLI and deployment command at a pinned SHA
Classify every tracked Python file and inline interpreter call as backend/runtime, backend-coupled tooling/test, client-only, or historical evidence; assign a migration owner
Create a change ledger for main changes during the rewrite and a per-capability parity matrix
acceptance: All 51 registered adapters and all current MCP registry entries are accounted for, with zero unowned production capabilities
Each Python file has a disposition; client-only means no backend imports, embedded server or FFI/subprocess fallback
Record omitted/null/empty/error semantics and mandatory tests; new upstream changes cannot silently fall outside the matrix
items.handoff: Versioned capability and Python-disposition manifests, baseline SHA and drift-update procedure; prerequisite for architecture sign-off.

items.title: Decide Rust crate boundaries, storage compatibility and transport policy
items.problem: Cold implementers need one agreed application boundary rather than incompatible Rust designs in each lane.
scope: Write ADRs for domain/application/infrastructure/HTTP/MCP/native-client boundaries; retain Valkey as the only shared authority
Pin candidate toolchain/crates and decide adapter registration, dependency injection, schema representation, TLS and supported platforms
Preserve all advertised transports including SSE unless a separate maintainer decision explicitly retires it; choose mixed-version records versus drain-and-migrate
Document immutable evidence ownership, mutable execution state and validated dispatch/commit authority
acceptance: ADRs enumerate compatibility decisions and unresolved risks with owner roles and decision gates
No Python runtime, PyO3 backend, Python sidecar or hidden interpreter fallback is part of the final design
Wire compatibility is independent of internal Rust types; storage rollback readers/writers have an explicit strategy
items.handoff: Accepted interface/storage/transport ADRs and version pins used by all implementation lanes.

items.title: Add Cargo workspace and minimal native CI smoke

Add a native readiness smoke that runs with no Python executable on PATH
Define documented cargo xtask check <plan-id> entrypoints for each lane; acceptance must fail for missing fixtures/unimplemented cases and produce machine-readable evidence, not count-only success.

Define minimal metrics/audit/supervisor interfaces with no-op/test sinks. F14/workflows own task lifecycles and emit through these seams; O01 adds production exporters/retention; G01/G02 verify complete integration.
acceptance: Clean checkout builds and tests the Rust skeleton on supported development/CI targets
Smoke invokes a compiled executable and proves no Python subprocess/import bridge
Existing Python paths stay operational until explicit cutover; crate ownership and developer commands are documented
items.handoff: Buildable Rust workspace, CI commands and injection seams; not a claim of feature parity.
